title: Dining Philosophers: A Deadlock by Symmetry
topic: Dining philosophers — five threads each need two shared chopsticks; if every philosopher grabs the left one first they all wait forever for the right. The four Coffman conditions for deadlock and how breaking symmetry breaks the cycle.

beats.narration: Five philosophers, five chopsticks, one round table. They take turns thinking and eating — but their lock pattern can stop them all at once.

elements.content: Five threads, five locks — a textbook deadlock waiting to happen.

beats.narration: Each philosopher needs the chopstick on their left and the one on their right at the same time. To pick one up they must grab a lock that no neighbour holds.

elements.content: rule — eat needs both adjacent chopsticks
Five philosopher nodes evenly spaced around a circle with a chopstick (locked resource) between each pair

beats.narration: Suppose every philosopher reaches for the left chopstick first, at the same moment. They all succeed. Then each turns to grab the right — and finds a neighbour holding it. Nobody can finish. Nobody lets go. Deadlock.

elements.content: Each philosopher's left arm extends out to grab its left chopstick; chopsticks become rose; then right arms reach but stop short — frozen mid-reach

beats.narration: Coffman's four conditions name what just happened. Mutual exclusion. Hold and wait. No preemption. And a circular wait around the table.

elements.content: The five hold-arrows redrawn as a directed cycle around the table; four labels appear pointing at corresponding visual features

beats.narration: Break any one and the gridlock dissolves. One classic fix: number the chopsticks and always pick the lower-numbered one first. One philosopher reverses, and the cycle never closes.

elements.content: always pick the lower-numbered chopstick first
One philosopher's reach order swaps — instead of left first they go right first; the cycle visibly breaks at that link, others can complete
